webtools.name: Web & Node tools
webtools.section.name: Web & Node tools
webtools.section.title: Web & Node tools
webtools.section.desc: Static helpers for CSS and SCSS, React, Node backends and .env files. Each tool shows up only in a repository that has the files it works on.
webtools.section.enableDesc: The tools only read your files; nothing is changed, deleted or sent anywhere. Try it talks to a dev server on this computer only. Check dependencies runs only after you confirm it.
webtools.noRepoDesc: Add a repository to the workspace to see what these tools find in it.
webtools.nothingDesc: This repository has no stylesheets, React files, Node backend, .env files, build output or package.json.
webtools.ask.unavailable: The New run dialog is not available.
webtools.conf.tip: How sure this static check is. Names built at run time, templates and libraries can hide a use, so always read the suggestion before you accept it.
webtools.tokens.title: Design tokens
webtools.tokens.intro: Your colours, spacings and fonts written once as CSS custom properties (--brand) or SCSS variables ($brand), and where each one is used. Nothing is changed.
webtools.tokens.noneDesc: Define colours as :root '{' --brand: #5b8def '}' or $brand: #5b8def and they will be listed here.
webtools.tokens.unusedWhy: These tokens are defined but nothing refers to them with var(--name) or $name. Removing them keeps your design file short and honest.
webtools.tokens.dynamic: Some names are built at run time (for example var(--$'{name}')), so a token marked unused may still be used.
webtools.tokens.askUnusedAria: Ask the agent to check and remove the unused tokens
webtools.tokens.hardcoded: Values that could use a token
webtools.tokens.hardcodedWhy: These colours and sizes are typed by hand but equal an existing token. Using the token means one change later instead of many.
webtools.tokens.askHardcoded: Ask agent to use the tokens
webtools.tokens.askHardcodedAria: Ask the agent to replace these hand-typed values with tokens
webtools.tokens.duplicatesWhy: The same colour under two token names, or written by hand many times. One name per colour keeps the design consistent.
webtools.tokens.dupHand: {count, plural, one {written by hand # time} other {written by hand # times}}
webtools.tokens.askDupAria: Ask the agent to merge the colour {value}
webtools.styles.title: Unused styles
webtools.styles.intro: Class selectors that exist in your CSS or SCSS but that no component or page seems to use. Nothing is ever deleted by this tool.
webtools.styles.dynamicNote: Some class names are built at run time, so the ones marked unused are less sure.
webtools.styles.noneDesc: Every class defined in your stylesheets is used somewhere.
webtools.styles.askAria: Ask the agent to review the unused classes in {file}
webtools.styles.neverDeletes: Classes used only by third-party code, by a template this scan cannot read, or by a name put together at run time can show up here by mistake. Check before you remove one.
webtools.react.title: React checks
webtools.react.intro: Common accessibility and structure problems found by reading your .tsx and .jsx files. These are heuristics: the files are read, not run, so check each place before you change it.
webtools.react.heuristicTip: Found by reading the code text, not by running the app. Some findings can be false alarms.
webtools.react.askAllAria: Ask the agent to fix all: {rule}
webtools.react.askAria: Ask the agent to fix {file} line {line}
webtools.react.imgAlt.title: Images without alt text
webtools.react.imgAlt.why: Screen readers read the alt text aloud, and it shows when the image does not load. Without it, blind visitors do not know what the image is.
webtools.react.noAccessibleName.title: Buttons and links with no readable text
webtools.react.noAccessibleName.why: An icon-only button needs a name (aria-label) so people using a screen reader or voice control know what it does.
webtools.react.inputLabel.title: Inputs without a label
webtools.react.inputLabel.why: A placeholder is not a label. Without a label, a screen reader cannot tell what to type, and clicking the text does not focus the field.
webtools.react.clickNonInteractive.title: Clicks on elements the keyboard cannot reach
webtools.react.clickNonInteractive.why: A clickable div or span cannot be reached with the Tab key or used with Enter. A real button works for everyone.
webtools.react.listKey.title: Lists without a key
webtools.react.listKey.why: React needs a stable key on each list item to update the right one. Without it you can get wrong or slow updates and lost input.
webtools.react.fragmentKey.title: List items in a fragment without a key
webtools.react.fragmentKey.why: A short fragment <></> cannot carry a key. Use <React.Fragment key='{...}'> when a list returns a fragment.
webtools.react.largeComponent.title: Very large components
webtools.react.largeComponent.why: Long components are hard to change without breaking something, for you and for the agent. Splitting them gives smaller, safer pieces.
webtools.react.manyProps.title: Components with many props
webtools.react.manyProps.why: A component that takes many props usually does too much. Grouping props or splitting the component makes it easier to reuse.
webtools.bundle.title: Bundle size
webtools.bundle.intro: The biggest files in an existing build output (dist, build, .next, out). This reads what is already built; it never runs a build.
webtools.bundle.noneDesc: Run your build once (for example npm run build) and open this again.
webtools.bundle.gzipTip: A typical ratio per file type, not a measurement: text files shrink to about a third, images and fonts hardly shrink.
webtools.bundle.built: Newest file built {when}. If you changed code since, build again to see current sizes.
webtools.bundle.maps: Source maps ({size}) are not counted: visitors do not download them.
webtools.bundle.ask: Ask agent to slim it down
webtools.bundle.askAria: Ask the agent to reduce the size of {dir}
webtools.routes.title: Backend routes
webtools.routes.intro: The HTTP routes your Node backend declares (Express, Fastify, Koa, Hono, NestJS, Next.js), found by reading the code. Nothing is started.
webtools.routes.noneDesc: Routes written as app.get('/path', ...) or as Next.js route files are listed here.
webtools.routes.askAria: Ask the agent to review these routes
webtools.routes.caveat: Paths are shown as written in each file. A prefix added where a router is mounted (app.use('/api', router)) or a global prefix is not added, and a path built from a variable is not found.
webtools.try.title: Try it
webtools.try.intro: Send one request to a dev server that you started from the Scripts panel and look at the answer.
webtools.try.noServerDesc: Start your dev server from the Scripts panel. Try it only talks to servers started there.
webtools.try.loopback: Requests go only to 127.0.0.1 on this computer, never to another address, and redirects are shown but not followed. Anything you type here, including a token in a header, is sent to your own dev server and is not saved.
webtools.try.badPath: Write only a path that starts with one slash, like /api/users (no address, no spaces).
webtools.try.redirect: The server redirects to {to}. It was not followed; change the path to go there.
webtools.try.binary: The answer is not text ({bytes} bytes), so it is not shown.
webtools.try.truncated: The answer was longer than 256 KB; only the start is shown.
webtools.env.title: .env files
webtools.env.intro: Compares the variable names in .env.example with your real .env files and checks that the real ones cannot be committed. Values are never read into the app, shown, logged or put in a prompt.
webtools.env.noneDesc: Files named .env, .env.local or .env.example are compared here.
webtools.env.unprotectedWhy: No .gitignore rule covers this file, so a commit could include your secrets.
webtools.env.trackedWhy: Git already tracks this file, so its content is in the history. Treat its secrets as leaked and replace them.
webtools.env.noEnv: There is an example file but no real .env yet. Copy the example to .env and fill in your own values.
webtools.env.noExample: There is no .env.example. A file with the names (and empty values) helps everyone, including the agent, know what to set.
webtools.env.missingWhy: Listed in the example file but missing from your .env, so the app may fail to start or behave oddly:
webtools.env.undocumentedWhy: In your .env but not in the example file, so a new teammate would not know about them:
webtools.env.askAria: Ask the agent to fix the env files in {dir}
webtools.deps.title: Dependencies
webtools.deps.intro: Runs npm outdated and npm audit to list packages that have newer versions and known security problems. It asks the npm registry over the internet, so it runs only when you press the button and confirm.
webtools.deps.noNpmDesc: This check needs a package.json with a package-lock.json.
webtools.deps.otherManager: This project uses {manager}, which this check does not support yet. Only npm projects can be checked.
webtools.deps.timeout: npm took too long and was stopped.
webtools.deps.askAria: Ask the agent to upgrade the packages safely
webtools.deps.confirmDesc: This runs npm in the project folder and contacts the npm registry.
webtools.deps.confirm1: npm outdated and npm audit are run once. Nothing is installed or changed.
webtools.deps.confirm2: The package names and versions of this project are sent to the npm registry (and to the registry set in your .npmrc, if any).
webtools.deps.confirm3: It stops by itself after 90 seconds.
webtools.inspect.title: Element styles
webtools.inspect.noRepo: This preview has no repository to search in.
webtools.inspect.noRule: No CSS rule with these classes, id or tag was found. The style may come from a library, an inline style or a component the scan cannot read.
webtools.inspect.noShot: No screenshot is attached: the preview cannot be captured from here.
